source_review.notes: Checked seven official sources. Current Grafana k6 documentation distinguishes open arrival-rate and closed virtual-user models, describes coordinated omission risk, ramping-arrival executors and threshold assertions. Current Prometheus guidance distinguishes aggregatable histograms from client-computed summaries and warns against aggregating precomputed quantiles. Google SRE guidance recommends empirical resource-to-capacity load testing, testing beyond rated capacity, graceful degradation/load shedding and recovery. Tool mechanisms are examples; workload fidelity, capacity criteria, safety, evidence and expiry remain explicit local policy.

evidence: Checked arrival/completion rate lambda, service rate mu, utilization rho, mean residence W and average population N.
Checked usable capacity C(x), replica capacity C(n), scaling efficiency eta(n), and separate offered/scheduled/started/admitted/good/rejected/failed/timeout/retry symbols.
Confirmed Little's Law is scoped to a consistent stable boundary and M/M/1 is explicitly an illustrative model rather than a deployed forecast.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Capacity is defined by a declared workload/configuration vector and quality constraints, not a universal scalar.

evidence: Recomputed 1,000 operations/s times 0.2 s as 200 average concurrent operations.
Recomputed M/M/1 W with mu=1000/s as 5 ms at lambda=800/s and 20 ms at 950/s.
Recomputed exercise concurrency 2400/s times 0.125 s as 300.
Recomputed scaling efficiencies: 330/(2x180)=0.917, 540/(4x180)=0.75 and 680/(8x180)=0.472.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All rates and timings are scenarios; deployed results require repeated empirical measurements and consistent units/windows.

evidence: Derived Little's Law by equating accumulated work-time through average population and completed work residence time.
Verified the M/M/1 denominator approaches zero as lambda approaches mu from below, illustrating nonlinear queue delay.
Constructed a stall during which a closed generator suppresses arrivals and confirmed it cannot represent a fixed independent arrival process.
Verified any load violating correctness, SLO, resource stability or recovery cannot satisfy the chapter's usable-capacity definition.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Queueing intuition motivates measurement; real concurrency, service distributions, multiple servers and feedback require empirical evidence.

evidence: Reviewed open, closed and hybrid models; logical operations, attempts, connections, streams, jobs/events; scheduled/dropped/admitted/completed/correct/retried/effect accounting.
Reviewed operation/payload/tenant/client/version/region/data-skew/cache/error mixes, correlated bursts, cold/warm state, auth/TLS/gateway/mesh and side-effect safety.
Reviewed generator CPU/network/ports/connections/VU/GC limits, shared-environment noise, dependencies, data/schema/config provenance and clock boundaries.

Reviewed warm-up/ramp/steady/spike/stress/breakpoint/soak/cooldown/recovery, autoscaling lag, rolling versions, shard imbalance, replica/zone loss, overload/shedding/degradation, retries, leaks/compaction and persistent backlog.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans workload, generator, client path, state, topology, resources, dependencies, time, overload, failure, scaling, recovery, comparison and decisions.

evidence: Confirmed each capacity claim binds exact workload, artifacts, configuration, data, topology, dependencies, resources, generator and pass/fail windows.
Confirmed scheduled, started, dropped, admitted, correct, rejected, failed, timeout, retry and effect measurements stay distinct and include unsuccessful latency/outcomes.
Confirmed correctness and security invariants continue under load and generator/environment limitations cannot be attributed to SUT capacity.
Confirmed safe capacity requires stable slopes, SLO/resource guardrails, overload behavior, recovery, fault headroom, repetitions, uncertainty, cost and expiry.
invariant_checking.notes: Maximum throughput, breakpoint and a short plateau are explicitly insufficient capacity evidence.

evidence: Reviewed Little's Law accounting and stable-boundary assumptions.
Reviewed queueing-knee illustration and confirmed its limited model claim.
Reviewed coordinated-omission counterexample and the difference between closed feedback and open arrivals.
Reviewed safe-capacity argument against throughput-only definitions.
proof_review.notes: Formal results structure experiments; the actual knee, bottleneck, scaling, recovery and capacity envelope require measurement.

evidence: Confirmed formal passages are labeled Little's Law accounting, queueing-knee illustration, coordinated-omission counterexample and safe-capacity argument.
Confirmed k6, Prometheus and Google SRE claims remain scoped to official sources.
Confirmed workload models, thresholds, headroom, resource guardrails, scaling and capacity expiry are architectural/operating choices.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Models, tool behavior, empirical claims and local policy remain separate.

evidence: All seven official references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current documentation applies.

The chapter requires raw distributions, repetitions/variance, exact artifact/config/data/topology/dependency/generator provenance, scheduled/drop accounting, resource/queue/dependency telemetry, correctness/effects, overload/recovery and cost evidence.
No production API's latency, capacity, scalability, cost, overload safety or recovery readiness is asserted.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Worked examples and calculations illustrate experiment interpretation, not benchmark claims.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed falsifiable claims, demand modeling, open/closed models, Little's Law/queueing, generator validation, phases/steady state, distributions/useful work, bottlenecks/knees, overload/recovery, scaling/topology, soak, controlled comparison and capacity decisions as one empirical discipline.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through production-derived safe mixes, exact manifests, generator calibration, open arrival accounting, client-path fidelity, phase-labeled histograms, invariant sampling, per-shard/resource telemetry, step ramps, overload/failure/recovery tests, autoscaling-lag measurement, soak slopes, alternating repeated comparisons and capacity/headroom/runbook outputs.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module develops claims and workload first, then models, generator validity, phases, measurements, knees, overload, scaling, soak, comparison and decisions. Counterexamples expose maximum-RPS-equals-capacity, users-equal-arrivals, success-only-latency, average-p99 and plateau-equals-sustainable shortcuts. Ten examples and five progressive exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external performance engineer, SRE, capacity planner, tool vendor, platform, database, or practitioner review is claimed.
